To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the selector devices play a crucial role in obtaining the high performance cross point RRAM memory arrays.

we have demonstrated the first ever cross point memory device with 10 ^{8} ON/OFF ratio, low power consumption (0.2V, 10µA) and good retention and endurance (10 ^{6} cycles) using the novel 1S1RRAM structure.

various self-rectification cells and selector devices were studied for cross point RRAM arrays and it is observed that 1S1D devices have better performance in terms of endurance, retention and operating voltage than SRC and it is also observed that selector devices with high on/off ratio and low operating voltage can be used for obtaining better performance cross point memory array.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel 1S1 RRAM devices with excellent device performance.

the fabrication of cross point RRAM arrays using various self-rectification techniques and selector devices to obtain the high density, low power, and low voltage operation for future memory applications.
the fabrication, characterization, and understanding the mechanism of various selector devices and their integration with cross point memory arrays to overcome the sneak-path problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self-rectification in RRAM devices is still a challenging task and there is no single device which can overcome the sneak path problems in cross point arrays.
, 1S1 R cross point memory arrays are more attractive than the SRC due to large possibilities of optimization to obtain the best device performance.
, the cross point RRAM arrays are still under development and the research in the field is still going on to achieve the best performance for the future memory devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selector devices are the key to achieve high performance 3-D stack able cross point RRAM arrays.
we have developed a new kind of selector device based on metal oxide and we have also demonstrated the 1S1D cross point memory array using the developed selector device.

we have demonstrated the first 1S1D and 1S1M cross point memory devices using Si-based selector device and demonstrated the first 2S1R cross point memory device using metal-oxide based threshold switch selector device.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-rectified cross point memory arrays are the promising candidates for future non-volatile memories.
the 3-D stack cross point memory arrays are possible to be fabricated by using the self-rectified cells and selector devices.
the 3-D stackability of the memory array is possible only with the help of selector devices.
